prompt: Since midnight the DNS record for the box office points at the wrong address. What do lesson 22's metrics show?

choices.text: A quiet night: the requests never arrive
choices.why: Right. The server counts what it answers; requests sent elsewhere leave nothing to count.

choices.text: A rise in 5xx answers on every route
choices.why: A 5xx is something the server answered; here it answers nothing.

choices.text: up dropping to 0 for the boxoffice job
choices.why: Prometheus scrapes 127.0.0.1 directly and still reaches the process, so up stays at 1.

choices.text: A spike of requests from the wrong address
choices.why: The customers' requests go to the wrong machine, not to this one from somewhere odd.

prompt: Which of these does real-user monitoring see and a synthetic check does not?
hint: One of them walks only the journey somebody wrote.

choices.text: An outage at 04:00 with nobody using the site
choices.why: That is the synthetic check's strength; real-user data is silent when nobody is there.

choices.text: Slow pages on phones in one country
choices.why: Right. Those devices and that network are not anything the probe uses.

choices.text: The same journey timed identically every minute
choices.why: Repeatability is what the probe has and real traffic lacks.

choices.text: A booking that answers 201 in 916 ms
choices.why: The probe caught exactly that in this lesson.

prompt: Runscope's checks ended up inside BlazeMeter after two changes of owner. What does that history argue for?
hint: Who owns the format your checks are written in?

choices.text: Never using a hosted product for anything
choices.why: Hosted checks give you regions you do not own; the point is keeping the definitions portable.

choices.text: Load testing and monitoring being the same activity
choices.why: The two products were put side by side; that says nothing about the activities being one.

choices.text: Checks kept as files in your own repository
choices.why: Right. A probe in a file moves with you; checks in a product's format move when the product does.

choices.text: Buying from the largest vendor available
choices.why: Runscope was bought by large vendors; that is what moved it.

prompt: GET /shows answers 200 with an empty list. Which of the probe's three checks catches it?

choices.text: The status
choices.why: 200 is the status it wanted.

choices.text: The time
choices.why: An empty list comes back fast.

choices.text: None of the three
choices.why: The body check exists for exactly this.

choices.text: The body
choices.why: Right: the probe refuses an empty list with "no show on sale".

prompt: Why does the probe try another seat after a 409, instead of failing?
hint: What does a 409 say about the box office?

choices.text: Somebody real has that seat
choices.why: Right. Failing on it would page somebody for a correct refusal.

choices.text: A 409 is a server failure the probe should hide
choices.why: It is not a failure at all: a real customer has the seat.

choices.text: urllib turns every 409 into a timeout
choices.why: urllib raises HTTPError, which call() turns back into the status 409.

choices.text: The probe's thresholds do not apply to bookings
choices.why: Bookings have a limit of their own, 500 ms.

prompt: Why are the probe's limits per request looser than a 95th-percentile requirement would be?

choices.text: urllib adds a fixed cost of its own to every request it sends
choices.why: The client's time is what a customer waits; the reason is variation, not a constant.

choices.text: One unlucky request is not a failure of the system
choices.why: Right. One slow request in twenty is inside a p95 requirement and would still fail a tight probe.

choices.text: Production is always slower than the lab it was tested in
choices.why: Not a rule; and the limit is about one request against a distribution.

choices.text: Percentiles do not apply in production
choices.why: They apply everywhere; lesson 22 computed them from production-style metrics.

prompt: What is the probe's exit code for?

choices.text: To count how many seats the journey managed to book
choices.why: It says pass or fail, nothing about how many.

choices.text: To report how long the slowest of the three steps took
choices.why: The times are in the printed line; the code is only 0 or 1.

choices.text: To say pass or fail without the line being read
choices.why: Right. 0 or 1 is what a loop, cron or lesson 24's alerting can act on.

choices.text: To release booking_lock on the server
choices.why: The probe is another process; it cannot touch the server's lock.

prompt: A probe runs every 60 seconds and somebody is told after two failed checks in a row. An outage starts just after a check. About how many minutes pass before somebody is told, at worst?
Under slow.py every answer was a 200 or a 201. Why would an alert on the 5xx ratio have said nothing?
hint: What failed: the answer or the wait?

choices.text: Prometheus does not scrape slow.py
choices.why: slow.py serves the same /metrics as observed.py.

choices.text: The probe's own requests are left out of the ratio
choices.why: They are counted like any other; none of them was a 5xx.

choices.text: A 201 counts as an error in the 5xx query
choices.why: status=~"5.." matches only 500 to 599.

choices.text: The booking succeeded, just in 916 ms
choices.why: Right. Slowness is a duration problem; an error ratio cannot see it.

prompt: Of the five fields at the start of a crontab line, the first one is the ___.
hint: The order runs from the smallest unit to the day of the week.

prompt: Why is watch -n 60 python3 probe.py not a monitor?
hint: What happens when you close the terminal?

choices.text: It keeps no history and dies with its terminal
choices.why: Right. Good for looking while you work; cron runs with no terminal and keeps the results.

choices.text: It cannot run Python programs
choices.why: It runs any command; that is not the problem.

choices.text: Sixty seconds is too short an interval for a production check
choices.why: One minute is the usual interval for a production check.

choices.text: It hides the probe's exit code from the screen it draws
choices.why: The exit code was never on the screen; the issue is where the results go.

prompt: The probe books once a minute and nobody cleans up. What happens to the box office?
hint: 1,440 bookings a day, into the same table.

choices.text: Nothing, since the probe's bookings are marked
choices.why: A mark lets you find them; it does not give the seats back.

choices.text: The first show sells out; then every check fails
choices.why: Right. The monitor causes the outage it reports, and real customers lose those seats first.

choices.text: The bookings slow down because of booking_lock
choices.why: One booking a minute is nothing next to the lock's 25 a second.

choices.text: SQLite refuses rows from a customer that is not a person
choices.why: The database stores any string as a customer.

prompt: Match each pattern of results to where it points.
hint: The figure of three regions, and the slow version.

pairs.right: the network path from that region

pairs.left: probes pass, one browser's users cannot pay

prompt: What is the better way to clean up a probe's bookings in production?
hint: Who should need write access to the sales table?

choices.text: An operator runs DELETE at a prompt whenever they remember
choices.why: That is what was done in the lab, and it is exactly what not to do in production.

choices.text: Leave them, and subtract the probe from every report
choices.why: The seats are still gone, and every report has to remember.

choices.text: A reviewed job or endpoint for the test customer
choices.why: Right. Nobody needs write access to the sales table, and the cleanup keeps pace with the probe.

choices.text: Stop the probe once a week to let the seats free up
choices.why: Stopping it frees nothing; the bookings stay until deleted.

prompt: The probe runs on the server's own machine and is green all night, yet customers report that the site will not open. What should change first?
hint: What lies between a customer and 127.0.0.1?

choices.text: Tighten the thresholds from 300 and 500 down to 100 ms
choices.why: The probe is fast and green; a tighter limit still never leaves the machine.

choices.text: Run the same probe at ten-second intervals instead of one minute
choices.why: More checks of the same path from the same place see the same thing.

choices.text: Add a body check to the listing step
choices.why: It already has one, and it passes on the machine itself.

choices.text: Probe the public address, from outside, from several regions
choices.why: Right. DNS, certificates, the balancer and the network are only crossed by a check that starts where customers are.

prompt: Put the probe's run in order, from start to what a scheduler sees.
hint: The journey first, then the verdict.
items: GET /shows, checked for status, body and time
one line saying PASS or FAIL

prompt: A team has a synthetic check every minute and no real-user monitoring. Which failure will they hear about from a customer first?
hint: Which of these does the scripted journey not walk?

choices.text: Accented searches finding nothing
choices.why: Right. The probe never searches, so only a person meets it, unless RUM or the error ratio shows it.

choices.text: The server stopping at 04:00 with nobody on the site
choices.why: The next check fails within a minute.

choices.text: Payments taking 900 ms each, all afternoon
choices.why: The booking step's time limit fails on it, as it did here.

choices.text: GET /shows answering with an empty list
choices.why: The body check refuses an empty list.

prompt: Which of these would the probe from this lesson catch? Choose every one it would.
hint: It lists, opens the first show and books.

choices.text: the server not running
choices.why: Yes: connection refused, exit 1.

choices.text: a booking that takes 916 ms
choices.why: Yes: over its 500 ms limit.

choices.text: the search route failing with 500
choices.why: No: the journey never searches.

choices.text: an empty list of shows answered with 200
choices.why: Yes: the body check refuses it.

choices.text: the last show on sale having a broken page
choices.why: No: it only opens the first show.
